prompt: A vertical 9:16 film photograph taken from the very back of a British ambulance at night, looking forward down the length of the patient compartment towards the cab and its windscreen. In the lower left foreground, out of focus and cut by the frame edge, a patient lies on the stretcher under a pale cellular blanket, an oxygen mask over their face, one arm still at their side. A tired paramedic in a dark green uniform kneels beside them in the middle of the frame, one gloved hand resting on the blanket, her head turned away from the patient to look forward through the cab. Beyond her, through the narrow gap between the two front seats, the windscreen fills the upper third: rain beading on the glass, a red traffic light blooming into the drizzle, the blurred red tail lights of a stopped queue of cars, and the silhouette of the driver's shoulder. Focus falls on the kneeling paramedic; the patient is soft and the windscreen view melts into haze. Light comes from a cold white overhead strip in the compartment, dimmed and greenish, while the red of the traffic light washes faintly along the ceiling and blue beacon spill flickers through the rear side window. Everything else drops to teal-black. Shot handheld with a slight tilt on a 35mm lens, CineStill 800T pushed two stops, red halation round the traffic light, visible grain, underexposed with lifted blacks. Her face has natural skin texture and the drawn look of a long shift, mouth closed. Thanks.
